title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
spaceBreakdown:
- no containers/arrays allocated
- no recursion (iterative loop)
- not counted: input vector `nums`, returned int
approach: The rotated sorted array consists of two increasing segments; the minimum is the only element smaller than its right neighbor (or the first element if no such drop exists). Use binary search comparing `nums[mid]` with `nums[hi]`: if `nums[mid] > nums[hi]`, the drop (and minimum) lies strictly to the right, so set `lo = mid + 1`; otherwise the minimum is at `mid` or to its left, so set `hi = mid`. When `lo == hi`, `nums[lo]` is the minimum. This is correct because the comparison cleanly partitions the array into the "rotated high part" and the "original low part" containing the minimum.
hints: The array is two increasing runs glued at one "drop" point. Where must the minimum element sit relative to that drop? The constraint n ≤ 5000 with a required O(log n) time rules out scanning every element.
Binary search. Compare the middle element with the rightmost element: in [4,5,6,7,0,1,2], mid value 7 > right value 2, so the minimum must be to the right of mid.

**Single element** - n = 1, the loop body never executes.
`Input: [5]` → `Expected: 5`
⚠️ Bug: using `while (lo <= hi)` with `lo = mid + 1` on the equal case → accesses `nums[1]`, out of bounds.

**Two elements, descending** - the drop is between the only two elements.
`Input: [2,1]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: writing `lo = mid` instead of `lo = mid + 1` → lo stays 0, hi stays 1, mid stays 0 forever (infinite loop).

**Minimum in the middle** - the minimum is not at either endpoint.
`Input: [3,1,2]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: writing `hi = mid - 1` instead of `hi = mid` → lo=0,hi=2,mid=1, nums[1]=1 < nums[2]=2 so hi=0, returns nums[0]=3 instead of 1.

**Already sorted (rotated n times)** - no drop exists, minimum is at index 0.
`Input: [11,13,15,17]` → `Expected: 11`
⚠️ Bug: comparing `nums[mid]` with the moving `nums[lo]` and doing `lo = mid + 1` when greater → lo marches past the end, out-of-bounds access.

followUps.q: What if duplicates are allowed in the array?
followUps.a: When `nums[mid] == nums[hi]`, you cannot tell which side holds the minimum, so decrement `hi` by one and continue. Worst case (all elements equal) degrades to O(n) time; space stays O(1).

followUps.q: Return the index of the minimum (the rotation count) instead of its value.
followUps.a: Run the identical binary search, but return `lo` rather than `nums[lo]`. Time remains O(log n) and space O(1).

followUps.q: Search for a specific target value in the rotated array.
followUps.a: At each step determine which of the two halves `[lo, mid]` and `[mid, hi]` is strictly increasing, then check whether the target lies inside that sorted half to decide which side to keep. Time O(log n), space O(1).
